findings.quoted_text: EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES.

EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES.
findings.explanation: Your liability is generally capped at the fees paid, but obligations under the independent contractor section are excluded from this limit, leaving your liability for those matters uncapped.
findings.suggested_change: Contractor's maximum liability to Company arising for any reason relating to Contractor's performance of Services under a Statement of Work shall be limited to the amount of fees paid to Contractor for the performance of such services.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body: Hello. I am writing to share a quick thought regarding the agreement before we sign. - Regarding the relevant clause, the current draft excludes certain obligations from the liability cap, which leaves liability uncapped for those matters. I propose modifying this section so that the maximum liability is consistently limited to the fees paid for the services. Thank you for your time.
